claims.claim: content_matches is an assertion type
content_matches takes params.pattern as a regular expression string
params.message is accepted on content_matches
An anchored pattern ^The capital of France is Paris\.$ rejects the paraphrase 'Paris is the capital of France.' (regex match is whole-string when anchored, not fuzzy)
content_includes is an assertion type
content_includes takes params.patterns as a list of strings
content_includes params.patterns also accepts a single scalar string (example patterns: 'Paris' with no list)
content_includes requires all listed patterns to be present (implicit AND across the list)
A regex alternation inside content_matches passes if any one of the alternatives is present
content_matches treats pattern as a regular expression (Regular Expressions section)
The pattern ^.{100}$ matches exactly 100 characters of response, so it can be used for an exact length check
The pattern ^.{50,200}$ enforces a 50 to 200 character length range via content_matches
The pattern ^.{50,}$ enforces a minimum length of 50 characters
content_matches supports the (?i) inline case-insensitive regex flag
is_valid_json is an assertion type
is_valid_json accepts params.message
json_schema is an assertion type
json_schema takes params.schema holding a JSON Schema object (type, properties, required)
json_schema property type 'integer' is a valid JSON Schema type accepted by the validator
json_schema enforces the 'format: email' keyword on the email property
The example apiVersion value is promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1
The example kind value is Scenario
Scenario resources have metadata.name
Scenario spec accepts a task_type field, and 'extraction', 'security' and 'test' are used as values in examples
Scenario spec accepts a description field
Scenario spec accepts a turns list
Each turn accepts role and content fields
Each turn accepts an assertions list whose items have type and params
A turn's role is user or a self-play role ID; promptarena validate rejects role: assistant.
The YAML example pattern "(^#{1,6} |\*\*|\*|`|\[.*\]\(.*\))" is a valid double-quoted YAML scalar (contains backslash-star escapes)
The example pattern ```python[\s\S]*?``` matches a fenced Python code block in response content
content_matches supports negative lookahead (?!...) so that ^(?!.*(inappropriate|offensive|harmful)).*$ fails when a banned word is present
content_matches regex supports word boundary \b and character class api[_-]?key within negative lookahead examples
content_not_includes is an assertion type
Conversation-level assertions exist and are distinct from per-turn assertions
content_not_includes accepts params.patterns
The no-pii-leakage example is a valid Scenario document (apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, spec.task_type, spec.description, spec.turns with assertions)
The SSN and credit-card regexes in the no-pii-leakage example are patterns that a content_matches assertion evaluates against the response
The context-retention example is a valid Scenario document
In the context-retention example, turns is indented four spaces under spec (after task_type at two spaces), which is malformed YAML and does not parse
An assertion placed on a role: user turn is evaluated against the assistant reply to that turn
llm_judge is an assertion type
llm_judge accepts params.criteria, params.judge_provider and params.message
judge_provider value 'openai/gpt-4o-mini' is a valid provider/model reference (provider openai, model gpt-4o-mini)
rest_eval is an assertion type
rest_eval accepts params.url
rest_eval accepts params.headers as a map of header name to value
${EVAL_API_KEY} inside a rest_eval header value is expanded from the environment at run time
rest_eval accepts params.criteria and params.min_score (a float threshold such as 0.9)
json_path is an assertion type
json_path accepts params.jmespath_expression (a JMESPath query string)
The progressive-validation example uses apiVersion promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1, kind Scenario and metadata.name progressive-validation
In the progressive-validation example, the turns list is indented four spaces under spec, which is malformed YAML and does not parse
Multiple assertions on one turn combine with implicit AND: all must pass for the turn to pass
Arena does not support conditional assertions (an assertion cannot be gated on context variables)
Scenario entries accept a context.variables map (example sets user_tier)
The context-variable example is a top-level list of scenario entries that each have name, context and turns, a shape the Scenario schema accepts
An assistant-role turn can have assertions and no content field
Scenario spec accepts a runs field, and runs: 10 requests ten repetitions
Arena has no built-in statistical aggregation across runs; runs only repeats the scenario and results must be analysed externally
The patterns field can be given as a bare string (patterns: answer) and is accepted by the parser
is_valid_json is used with a top-level value: true key rather than under params
validation_tests is a top-level Scenario or config key with good_responses and bad_responses lists
An assertions key with no entries (null value) is valid and results in no assertions
Semantic validation can be implemented using custom validators, which Arena supports
Sentiment checks in the example are done with content_matches and content_includes only (no sentiment model)
llm_judge is run against the judge_provider model during the scenario run
External evaluation via rest_eval delegates the decision to a service at the configured URL
A negative-lookahead content_matches pattern passes only when none of the listed words appear in the response
content_not_includes is a conversation-level assertion type, i.e. it is valid in spec-level assertions as well as per turn
